unchanged_original_task.problem: Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, n>=2, with a smooth positive probability volume dV and dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. All potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives. For a smooth semipositive big real (1,1) background theta, define P_theta(f) as the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh v<=f (equivalently the a.e. obstacle convention with canonical regularization). Put u preceq phi when u<=phi+C, and u~phi for mutual bounded difference including common poles. Define P_theta[phi]=(lim_{C->infinity}P_theta(min(phi+C,0)))^*. An ordinary model reference is sup phi=0 and P_theta[phi]=phi. The standard admissible reference regime additionally requires a genuine envelope P_(epsilon theta)(phi) for some 0<epsilon<1. Then each bounded logarithmic density F has an ordinary-type solution MA_ext_theta(u)=c_phi(F)exp(F)dV with u~phi and scalar c_phi(F)>0 uniquely determined; potential uniqueness is not automatic. Set B_phi(F)=log c_phi(F). For F continuous define A_phi(F) as all Borel probabilities nu such that B_phi(G)<=B_phi(F)-integral(G-F)dnu for every G continuous. In the admissible regime B_phi is concave, decreasing, 1-Lipschitz, and B_phi(F+a)=B_phi(F)-a; A_phi(F) is nonempty compact convex and absolutely continuous with respect to dV. Generic singleton supports hold on a dense G_delta. The same bounded-type functional exists for arbitrary Hermitian theta and phi=0. Smooth strictly positive solution forms Omega=theta+dd^c u have the classical adjoint: a positive smooth weight rho with dd^c(rho Omega^(n-1))=0 and nu=rho Omega^n/integral rho Omega^n. Extended products for rough potentials are non-pluripolar products with the smooth-background corrections; a weighted product is not declared defined merely because a supporting probability exists. Original S07 asks, in singular-reference and degenerate-background admissible regimes, for hypotheses giving a singleton A_phi(F) and an approximation-independent adjoint of a meaningful weak linearized Monge-Ampere operator. Specify a product and a weight rho for dd^c(rho(theta+dd^c u)^(n-1))=0, its normalization and relation to the supporting probability, and prove independence of admissible approximation. If every smooth positive potential perturbation is Gauduchon, normalized Monge-Ampere measures already extend bounded adjoints and are continuous under bounded capacity convergence, including Gauduchon surfaces; repeating these cases is insufficient. Supporting probabilities and their weak stability already exist without defining the displayed product. Smooth-density singleton supports in the Hermitian zero-reference regime do not settle singular references, degenerate residuals or arbitrary unbounded potentials. Control of potentials alone does not control conformal multipliers. No candidate hypothesis, weak product, weight or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_task.completionCriteria: Prove new fully specified nonvacuous singular-reference or degenerate-background sufficient conditions for singleton supports and a well-defined weak adjoint with justified multiplication, normalization, operator identity and approximation independence, or give a verified obstruction to a proposed unrestricted assertion. State density regularity, singularity class, approximation class and all positivity/solvability assumptions explicitly. Mere generic uniqueness, a supporting probability without a weak product, a smooth-potential case or an existing bounded Gauduchon case does not solve the requested extension. Independently reconstruct the proof and check exact external premises at primary sources; retain the boundary of any restricted theorem.

regime of the normalization functional, determine when Aφ (F ) is a singleton and when its probabil-
ity is an approximation-independent adjoint of a weak linearized Monge–Ampère operator. Specify
a meaningful product and weight for

State of the art. Supporting probabilities and their stability are constructed without declaring
this product deﬁned. Generic uniqueness holds on a dense Gδ for each ﬁxed admissible reference.
Smooth potentials have the classical adjoint. If every smooth positive potential perturbation is

current_primary_application_judgment: BT82 bounded local recursion, symmetry and decreasing full proof apply after a common smooth strictly psh correction; continuous potentials and continuous complex Hessians identify actual products by uniform mollification and fixed smooth-background expansion. fresh_mathematical_judgment: Actual ordinary-model and smaller-background competitors precede every use of the supplied scalar/support framework. Full C(X) signed density curves establish stationarity without preserving the factorized density subclass. Heat-resolvent uniform graph approximation and independently reconstructed Green-kernel L2/spectral energy both prove uniqueness for finite signed measures. Uniform residual tensors and a positive determinant lower bound prove all three actual probability/current/weight limits. No rough multiplier product is inferred merely from a support. The strict-continuous residual and exact fixed divisor are explicit nonempty assumptions; target and model masses need not be equal.

clause_assessment.request: New nonvacuous singular or degenerate sufficient conditions
clause_assessment.answer: An explicit genuinely unbounded admissible ordinary logarithmic model on P1 times P1, with nonclosed theta and no smooth positive Gauduchon perturbation; the reference has an open degenerate horizontal region. Continuous factored positive densities produce an actual continuous strict residual solution, including a nonsmooth example.

clause_assessment.request: Meaningful weak operator, product, weight and normalization
clause_assessment.answer: The nonpluripolar first product is the actual continuous form Omega. Smooth rho=1/(2ab) multiplies it coefficientwise before support arguments; Q=rho Omega is closed and integral rho Omega^2=1. The measure derivative is 2 Omega wedge ddc h; its logarithmic generator is Delta1/A+Delta2/b.

clause_assessment.request: Singleton support on the full continuous density space
clause_assessment.answer: Every full supporting probability annihilates the generator by exact two-sided smooth-potential density curves. Signed-measure uniqueness and granted full-support nonemptiness identify A_phi(F)={A/a dW}. Every meaningful normalized nonnegative integrable weight is unique almost everywhere.

Every smooth strict residual approximation retaining the exact divisor and converging uniformly as tensors gives the same probability, actual weighted current and weak multiplier measure, without symmetry, derivative bounds or pointwise weight control. Heat/rotation regularizations and mixed perturbations prove nonemptiness.
